messages:
Sam (marketing): quick ask for the launch blog + cost appendix: can runtime run a tiny batching sweep? want to show how different batching configs affect p50/p95 and estimated token cost for the hero-serve profile. goal is a short table we can quote in the appendix + a small artifact pack.

Ravi (runtime): got it. what dimensions do you want? batch size, max_latency_ms (queueing), per-request arrival model? Also do you want both warmed and cold cache views?

Sam (marketing): yes to both warmed/cold. dimensions: batch_size (1,4,8,16), max_queue_ms (0,20,50), and two arrival patterns: steady 25 rps and spiky 100rps bursts. acceptance: warmed p95 at recommended config must be <= 350ms and quantized variant p95 increase <= 1.4x. for marketing we'll cite the best steady config that meets those constraints.

Sam (marketing): also need a simple cost column: estimate USD per 1M tokens using our internal cost model (include assumptions). 5 raw outputs per cell for quality spot-check.

Jordan (eng-runtime): plan: run a small grid across variants fp16 + int8-llm, cohorts cold vs warmed (prime=1k tokens + 6 followups), batch sizes [1,4,8,16], max_queue_ms [0,20,50], patterns: steady 25rps (10k samples) and burst (100rps for 60s). we'll collect per-request latency, queue_time_ms, tokens_out, status, seed. output: CSV, aggregated table, small notebook that computes cost/1M tokens under your cost assumptions, and 5 jsonl samples/cell. estimate ~3 hours.

Ravi (runtime): sample run commands:```bash
# steady, batched
curl -s -X POST https://bench.internal/run -d '{"model":"hero-batch","variant":"int8-llm","requests":10000,"seq":1024,"batch_size":8,"max_queue_ms":20,"arrival":"steady","traces":true}'
# burst
curl -s -X POST https://bench.internal/run -d '{"model":"hero-batch","variant":"fp16","burst_rps":100,"burst_dur_s":60,"batch_size":16,"max_queue_ms":50,"traces":true}'
```

Maya (product): add a tiny quality check: 5 samples per cell and a BLEU-lite similarity vs baseline. flag any sample where similarity < 0.6. also note whether batching changes output ordering or tokenization artifacts.

Jordan (eng-runtime): will include samples and a quick diff. quick Q: warm weights between variant runs? warming gives realistic latency; restart gives worst-case.

Sam (marketing): warm weights between variants is fine. keep cold cohort strictly no-cache. document everything in the runbook because marketing will footnote the methodology.

Ravi (runtime): scheduling now. bench-bot will post artifacts. quick note: queueing increases tail if batch sizes too large during bursts; we'll surface a recommended operating point that balances p95 and token-cost.

bench-bot: bench-job-2381112223 started by Ravi at 2026-04-10T16:14:00Z

Jordan (eng-runtime): if any quantized variant shows >20% p99 regression we'll auto-trigger a larger repro with fixed seeds (5k) to rule out sampling noise.

Sam (marketing): ideal: one-line PASS/FAIL against acceptance + CSV + cost notebook + jsonl samples by EOD+1. if timing tight we can accept morning+2 but need artifacts before content freeze. thanks :pray:
